title: Works for weeks, then after ~49 days every wait_ready() fails at once. Tap the bug.
explain: A 1 ms uint32_t tick wraps after about 49.7 days. If start is 0xFFFFFFF0, start + 100 wraps to 84, and millis() > 84 is true at once. This is a tick wraparound bug. Compare the elapsed time instead: millis() - start > TIMEOUT_MS. Unsigned subtraction gives the right result across the wrap.

title: enable_all() runs, but no ADC channel is ever enabled. Tap the bug.
explain: auto ch makes a copy of each element. The loop changes the copies, and the array stays the same. Use a reference: for (auto& ch : channels). Watch for this in config tables and driver state arrays. The compiler gives no error.

title: STM32 HAL. BME280 at 0x76 never ACKs. The wiring is fine. Tap the bug.
explain: STM32 HAL wants the 7-bit address shifted left by one. It puts the R/W bit in bit 0 itself. With 0x76 the bus sends address 0x3B, so nobody answers. Pass BME280_ADDR << 1. Check what each HAL expects: some take 7-bit, some take 8-bit addresses.

pr.title: Fix ADC average for 64 samples
pr.author: senior-fw
pr.body: 64 x 4095 = 262080 does not fit in uint16_t. The average is wrong at high input.

explain: Good change. A 12-bit ADC gives up to 4095. 64 samples sum to 262080, which needs 18 bits. The uint16_t sum wrapped, so a high input showed a low average. uint32_t holds the full sum, and the result after / 64 fits in uint16_t again.

pr.title: Build for Cortex-M0 (thumbv6m)
pr.author: junior-fw
pr.body: AtomicU32::swap does not exist on thumbv6m, so the build fails. Replace it with load + store. The ISR still increments COUNT.

explain: load and store are each atomic, but the pair is not. If the ISR increments COUNT between them, store(0) wipes that event. Cortex-M0 has no atomic read-modify-write instructions. Use critical_section::with around both steps, or the portable-atomic crate with its critical-section feature.

pr.title: Clear TIM2 flag after the work
pr.author: junior-fw
pr.body: Clear the update flag at the end of the ISR, so a new update during the work is not lost.

explain: On Cortex-M with STM32, the write to TIM2->SR goes through the bus and can finish after the ISR returns. The NVIC still sees the request and runs the ISR a second time. Clear the flag at the start. If you must clear it late, read SR back or add __DSB() after the write. A new update after an early clear sets the flag again, so nothing is lost.

title: What happens?
explain: Line 5 compiles. 300 is cut to 44 with at most a warning. Brace init does not allow narrowing. 300 does not fit in uint8_t, so line 6 is a compile error. Use brace init for register values and config constants. The compiler then catches values that do not fit.

title: Sum 16-bit LE words from a packet. What does this print?
explain: chunks_exact(2) gives [1,2] and [3,4]. 0x0201 + 0x0403 = 513 + 1027 = 1540. The last byte 5 goes to remainder() and is skipped with no error. Check remainder() or the length first, or the odd byte is lost.

title: 3.3 V MCU output drives a 74HC chip powered from 5 V. Is the logic HIGH safe?
options: No: 74HC needs about 3.5 V for HIGH at 5 V. Use 74HCT or a level shifter
No: 3.3 V will damage the 74HC input
Yes, if you add a 10 kΩ series resistor
explain: A CMOS 74HC input at 5 V needs VIH of about 0.7 × VCC = 3.5 V. A 3.3 V output is below that, so HIGH is not guaranteed. 74HCT has TTL levels (VIH = 2.0 V), so 3.3 V works. Or use a level shifter. A series resistor does not raise the voltage.

title: Tick counters and timeouts: 4 rules
bullets: Keep timestamps in a fixed unsigned type, like uint32_t. A 1 ms uint32_t tick wraps after about 49.7 days.
Compare elapsed time: now - start >= timeout. Unsigned subtraction is correct across the wrap.
Never compare a deadline: now > start + timeout breaks when start + timeout wraps.
In Rust, use now.wrapping_sub(start). Plain - panics in debug builds when it wraps.
Test it: start the tick counter near the wrap, for example at 0xFFFF0000.
